name: Robertson’s stiff chemical kinetics
description:
Robertson's three reactions, the classic stiff test problem ROBER: A → B at 0.04 per second, B + B → C + B at 3·10⁷, and B + C → A + C at 10⁴. Each reaction is a transfer whose rate reads the concentrations, so the diagram is the reaction scheme and the three compartments always add up to 1 (the Total expression). The intermediate B never exceeds 3.65·10⁻⁵, which it reaches after 4.6 ms; B_x_1e4 is B times 10⁴, the way it is usually plotted beside A and C.

The run covers seventeen decades of time, from a microsecond to 10¹¹ s, with twenty saved times a decade, and it ends within 10⁻⁷ of the published reference solution at t = 40 and at t = 10¹¹. The rate constants differ by nearly nine orders of magnitude, which is stiffness at its plainest: the NDF solver takes 1760 steps, while dp45 stalls before t = 3 and Tsit5 runs out of its ten million steps before t = 5000. The tolerances are tight (rtol 1e-8, abstol 1e-14) because B, and late in the run A, are numbers a looser absolute tolerance cannot see.
